context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS while supporting analyst reviews. It ensures strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a €25k monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- **Merchant / Payment Gateway**: External system submitting payment authorizations.
- **Fraud Analyst**: Human persona managing suspicious payments.
- **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System**: Core AWS-based system containing scoring engines and case management.
- **AWS KMS / S3 Object Lock**: Infrastructure providing WORM storage and encryption.
- **Identity Provider (IdP)**: External system managing OIDC/SAML authentication.

## Relationships
- Merchant/Gateway $\rightarrow$ Fraud System: Submits auth requests via gRPC over TLS 1.3 (<50ms P99).
- Fraud Analyst $\rightarrow$ Fraud System: Reviews flagged cases via HTTPS/TLS with OIDC/SAML MFA.
- Fraud System $\rightarrow$ AWS S3 Object Lock: Persists tamper-evident decisions using AWS SDK and IAM via AWS KMS.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Container orchestration chosen to minimize operational toil for a 3-person team.
- **gRPC / TLS 1.3**: Communication protocol ensuring ultra-low latency (<50ms P99).
- **AWS S3 Object Lock & KMS**: WORM storage and envelope encryption meeting 7-year audit requirements.
- **Terraform**: Infrastructure-as-Code for GitOps automated deployments.

## Rationale
Managed AWS services and containerization reduce operational overhead for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 boundaries. gRPC and serverless scalability meet high-throughput, low-latency requirements within the fixed €25,000 monthly budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and provides case management for analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and sub-50ms P99 latency within a fixed budget and small engineering team.

## Key Elements
- **Users:** Fraud Analyst, Merchant / Payment Gateway, Compliance & Risk Officer
- **External Systems:** AWS KMS, AWS S3 Object Lock, Identity Provider (IdP)
- **Containers:** API Gateway (AWS API Gateway), Scoring Engine (AWS Lambda with Provisioned Concurrency, Go runtime), Case Management (Node.js/React on ECS Fargate), Data Layer (Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL), Async Messaging (AWS SQS), Observability (AWS X-Ray)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway calls API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS for real-time payment authorization
- API Gateway communicates with Scoring Engine via gRPC using mTLS
- Scoring Engine asynchronously enqueues audit logs to AWS SQS
- Case Management connects to Aurora PostgreSQL for case review data
- Scoring Engine and Case Management retrieve secrets via AWS Secrets Manager and AWS KMS

## Technology Stack
- **Compute:** AWS Lambda with Provisioned Concurrency for Go-based stateless scoring; ECS Fargate for Node.js case management
- **Database & Storage:** Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL for transactional and audit data; S3 Object Lock for 7-year tamper-evident audit logs
- **Messaging:** AWS SQS for decoupled asynchronous audit event streaming
- **Security & Networking:** AWS API Gateway for edge tokenization via AWS KMS; AWS Secrets Manager for dynamic secret injection; IdP with OAuth2/OIDC for RBAC
- **Observability:** AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing and latency monitoring

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and fully managed AWS services to eliminate operational toil, fitting the constraints of a 3-person team and a €25k/month budget. Strict isolation of tokenized data at the edge and Lambda provisioned concurrency ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a sub-50ms P99 latency SLA.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time card-not-payment fraud screening for a mid-size payment processor and enables analysts to review suspicious transactions. It processes authorizations with sub-50ms latency while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a strict budget.

## Key Elements
- Merchants / Payment Gateways
- AWS API Gateway (HTTP APIs)
- AWS WAF
- Edge Tokenizer Lambda Component
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Scoring Engine (AWS Lambda, Go)
- Case Management (ECS Fargate, Node.js/React)
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL
- Fraud Analyst

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Submits payment authorizations [HTTPS/TLS, OAuth2/API Keys]
- AWS API Gateway -> AWS WAF: Inspects inbound traffic for threats [AWS WAF Integration]
- AWS API Gateway -> Amazon DynamoDB: Validates idempotency keys and throttling limits [AWS SDK]
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Forwards tokenized payloads for fraud evaluation [gRPC over mTLS]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL: Reads rules and stores immutable audit trails [PostgreSQL Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway (HTTP APIs): Edge routing, schema validation, and rate limiting within budget
- AWS WAF: Edge protection against DDoS and injection attacks without violating latency SLAs
- Amazon DynamoDB: Stateless idempotency and throttling tracking minimizing operational overhead for 3 engineers
- AWS Lambda (Go): High-performance edge tokenization and real-time scoring within 50ms P99 constraint
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL: Relational storage for case management and immutable audit logs

## Rationale
The serverless and managed AWS architecture meets the strict 50ms P99 latency and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance requirements while operating comfortably within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Furthermore, managed services minimize operational overhead, enabling a lean team of three engineers to maintain the platform securely.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Scoring Engine evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time while ensuring strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability. It processes requests with sub-50ms P99 latency within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget constraint.

## Key Elements
- **API Handler**: Go-based component using gRPC for inbound validation, correlation ID injection, and PAN data stripping.
- **Rule Evaluator**: Component for executing in-memory deterministic fraud rules via bytecodes.
- **Model Runner**: Component for evaluating lightweight probabilistic models using ONNX Runtime in Go with cryptographically signed artifact verification via AWS KMS.
- **Audit Logger**: Component that asynchronously batches and sends tamper-evident JSON audit payloads via internal Go channels.
- **Infrastructure Services**: AWS ECS Fargate on Graviton2 (ARM64), Amazon SQS, AWS Firehose, and Amazon S3 with Object Lock.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> API Handler**: Communicates scoring requests securely using gRPC with mTLS.
- **Model Runner -> AWS KMS**: Verifies cryptographic signatures of model artifacts retrieved from S3 prior to execution.
- **Audit Logger -> AWS SQS**: Asynchronously dispatches audit payloads using the AWS SDK for Go.
- **AWS SQS -> AWS Firehose -> Amazon S3**: Transports and archives immutable audit logs with S3 Object Lock compliance mode.

## Technology Stack
- **Go**: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency execution and optimal price-performance on ARM64.
- **AWS ECS Fargate on Graviton2 (ARM64)**: Provides scalable, cost-effective container orchestration without Lambda provisioning limits.
- **ONNX Runtime**: Enables fast in-memory probabilistic machine learning evaluations.
- **AWS KMS & S3 Object Lock**: Ensures cryptographic model verification and tamper-evident 7-year audit data retention.

## Rationale
This architecture uses ECS Fargate on Graviton2 and Go to consistently achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within the strict 25,000 EUR budget. Cryptographic verification, strict PAN sanitization, and immutable S3 Object Lock ensure full compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability constraints.

Case Management.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management system provides fraud analysts with an ECS Fargate and S3/CloudFront interface to review suspicious payment authorizations. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail for all human-in-the-loop decisions.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Case Management Container (ECS Fargate running Node.js)
- Analyst SPA (React hosted in S3 and served via Amazon CloudFront)
- API Router & Auth Component (Express.js)
- Case Workflow Engine with Prioritization Queue (Node.js)
- Audit Logger Component with AWS KMS integration (Node.js)
- Data Layer (Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL with Amazon RDS Proxy)
- AWS KMS and AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Analyst SPA: Reviews suspicious transactions [HTTPS/TLS via CloudFront]
- Analyst SPA -> API Router & Auth Component: Manages cases and submits overrides [HTTPS/REST with OAuth2/OIDC JWT]
- API Router & Auth Component -> Case Workflow Engine: Processes state transitions and prioritizes queues [In-memory function calls]
- Case Workflow Engine -> Audit Logger Component: Triggers audit events for analyst actions [In-memory function calls]
- Audit Logger Component -> AWS KMS: Generates cryptographic signatures for audit records [AWS SDK / IAM]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon RDS Proxy: Reads and writes case and audit data [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol via TLS]
- API Router & Auth Component -> AWS Secrets Manager: Injects secrets at startup [AWS SDK / IAM]

## Technology Stack
- React: Lightweight frontend SPA for rapid analyst workflows
- Node.js & Express.js: Low-overhead backend runtime for a three-engineer team
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Serverless container compute minimizing operational management
- Amazon S3 & CloudFront: Cost-effective static asset hosting staying within budget
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 with RDS Proxy: Auto-scaling relational storage with connection pooling
- AWS KMS: Cryptographic signing for tamper-evident 7-year audit logs

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team within a strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It strictly isolates sensitive card data via API tokenization while maintaining a tamper-evident audit trail for 7-year compliance.

Data Layer.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations and manages analyst reviews. It ensures strict PCI-DSS compliance, 7-year tamper-evident auditability, and sub-50ms P99 decision latency at 3,000 transactions per second.

## Key Elements
- Transactional Store: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL
- Feature Store: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless (Redis)
- Audit Ingestion Queue: Amazon SQS with Dead Letter Queue (DLQ)
- Security Controls: AWS KMS with customer-managed keys (CMK), AWS Secrets Manager, IAM Database Authentication
- Compliance Tools: Amazon S3 Object Lock, PostgreSQL pgAudit

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Reads velocity features [RESP, <5ms]
- Scoring Engine -> Async Messaging (SQS): Enqueues decision audit payloads [AWS SDK, HTTP/S]
- Case Management -> Transactional Store: Reads and writes analyst cases and reviews [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol, TLS 1.3]
- Transactional Store -> S3 Object Lock: Streams audit logs for tamper-evident 7-year retention [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL: Chosen for ACID compliance, relational case management, and scalable transactional throughput.
- Amazon ElastiCache Serverless (Redis): Chosen for sub-5ms real-time feature lookups without operational server management.
- Amazon SQS: Chosen to decouple synchronous scoring from database writes, ensuring P99 latency under 50 ms.
- AWS KMS: Chosen to enforce column-level encryption and zero exposure of plaintext card numbers (PAN).
- PostgreSQL pgAudit: Chosen to generate detailed security and compliance logs for PCI-DSS Level 1.

## Rationale
This architecture balances ultra-low latency requirements with strict financial compliance through asynchronous processing and high-performance in-memory caching. It maintains a lean operational footprint suited for a 3-engineer team while satisfying rigorous PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability mandates.

Async Messaging.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present authorizations and manages analyst reviews to ensure PCI-DSS compliance. Its core purpose is to score transactions in under 50 ms while maintaining an immutable, tamper-evident 7-year audit trail.]

## Key Elements
- Scoring Engine (AWS Lambda with Provisioned Concurrency, Go runtime)
- Async Messaging (Amazon SQS FIFO Queue and Dead-Letter Queue via AWS VPC Interface Endpoint)
- Data Layer (Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL)
- Case Management (Node.js / React on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Observability (Amazon CloudWatch, AWS X-Ray)
- Security (AWS KMS Customer Managed Key)

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine -> Audit Event FIFO Queue: Enqueues decision telemetry [HTTPS/TLS 1.3 via SQS API]
- Audit Event FIFO Queue -> Data Layer Worker: Persists immutable logs [AWS SDK internal polling / Internal TCP]
- Scoring Engine -> Data Layer: Queries rules and stores operational state [PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Case Management -> Data Layer: Manages review cases [PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3]
- CloudWatch -> PagerDuty: Alerts on queue age and DLQ depth [HTTPS webhooks]

## Technology Stack
- AWS SQS FIFO: High-throughput mode with message group IDs for ordered, exactly-once audit event processing
- AWS Lambda: Serverless compute for low-latency scoring and batched audit log ingestion
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL: Relational storage for transactions and case management
- AWS KMS: Customer Managed Keys with encryption context for data protection
- Node.js & Go: Runtime environments optimized for microservices and performance

## Rationale
[This architecture utilizes serverless and managed AWS services to scale dynamically and meet the strict 3,000 req/sec performance requirement within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It empowers a three-engineer team to maintain high availability, PCI-DSS compliance, and tamper-evident auditability without managing underlying infrastructure.]

Observability.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present payment authorizations under 50 ms while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and immutable auditability. It uses a cloud-native architecture on AWS to score transactions, manage fraud analyst reviews, and maintain strict operational visibility within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Merchant / Payment Gateway (External System)
- AWS API Gateway (Container)
- Scoring Engine: AWS Lambda with Provisioned Concurrency, Go runtime (Container)
- Case Management: Node.js / React on ECS Fargate (Container)
- Data Layer: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL (Container)
- Async Messaging: AWS SQS (Container)
- Observability: AWS X-Ray, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon SNS, S3 Object Lock (Container)
- Identity Provider - IdP (External System)
- AWS KMS / S3 Object Lock (External System)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Submits authorization requests [HTTPS / JSON]
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Invokes real-time fraud scoring [gRPC / AWS Lambda API]
- Scoring Engine -> Data Layer: Queries scoring models and rules [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS 1.3]
- Scoring Engine -> Async Messaging: Queues suspicious payments for review [AWS SQS API]
- Case Management -> Data Layer: Manages review cases and analyst actions [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS 1.3]
- Scoring Engine & Case Management -> Observability: Sends sanitized telemetry, traces, and logs [AWS X-Ray SDK, CloudWatch Agent / TLS 1.3]
- Observability -> S3 Object Lock: Exports audit logs for tamper-evident 7-year storage [AWS S3 API / TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Lambda & Go: Chosen for Scoring Engine to guarantee P99 latency under 50 ms at high throughput.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL: Provides auto-scaling relational data storage within budget constraints.
- AWS X-Ray & Amazon CloudWatch: Delivers distributed tracing, infrastructure metrics, and the Fraud Operations View.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Ensures 7-year tamper-evident WORM storage for PCI-DSS audit compliance.
- AWS KMS: Encrypts all data at rest using Customer Managed Keys.

## Rationale
This serverless and managed container architecture scales dynamically to handle 3,000 TPS within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget operated by three engineers. Fully managed AWS services minimize operational overhead while satisfying strict latency, PCI-DSS compliance, and immutable 7-year audit requirements.
